provider: EPrints 3.x platform class (White Rose, QUT, Southampton)

free_tier.stated: No quota model. EPrints has no per-user or per-collection byte accounting; the only constraints are the JavaScript max on the upload widget and Apache's LimitRequestBody.
free_tier.notes: the headline offer as the seed recorded it; the binding constraint is in limits[]

per_object_cap.stated: no per-object cap was extracted from the seed's quota and limits prose; absence here is a gap in this conversion, not a vendor claim that no cap exists
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: no retention statement was extracted from the seed's quota and limits prose; absence here is a gap in this conversion, not a vendor claim that retention is unlimited
retention.notes: extraction found no retention clause; the seed's limits text may still state one, see extras.limits_verbatim

egress.terms: Direct, no CDN in front on the instances checked.

tooling: SWORD client / curl POST to cgi/
chaining: Structurally unbounded, but the write gate is deposit-medated: White Rose's own registration page tells depositors to go through their university's CRIS (Symplectic, PURE, myPublications) instead of registering.
limits_note: Per-file only, set by Apache LimitRequestBody or the form's JS; practitioners on the EPrints list cite successful 50 GB uploads and advise against >10 GB because there is no resumable upload.
reliability_note: No resumable upload and no failure recovery — a >10 GB POST that drops must restart from zero.
confidence_note: mechanically converted from the seed corpus; no page was read for this record in the storage-dossier pass. One page read moves it to documented.

extras.agent_focus: Systematic sweep of self-hosted academic repository software (Dataverse, DSpace, InvenioRDM, EPrints, Fedora/Islandora) scored on the four client questions: institutional-email requirement, per-file cap, per-collection/dataset cap, and whether the install enforces a quota object at all. Primary method was machine probing, not page reading: /api/info/version and /api/dataverses/:root/storage/quota?showInherited=true against the full official Dataverse installation registry (150 hostnames), the native-signup form probe /dataverseuser.xhtml?editMode=CREATE against all 83 no-quota hosts, and the platform source defaults read out of the upstream config files for DSpace, InvenioRDM, EPrints, libp2p and iroh. Secondary coverage of the relay/P2P half of the slot.

binding_note: the quota is real and unreachable: identity is the binding constraint, and it is not one of the six limits kinds
